decisions.reason: The GPIO5 change applies to 5V_EN, not the separate GPIO13 charge-status LED signal or its connector circuit.
The addressable LEDs use the switched 5V rail, whose enable control necessarily changes from GPIO3 to GPIO5.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: That was my mistake: GPIO3 came from my original ESP32 design. Use GPIO5 for 5V_EN instead. I also realized that GPIO22, GPIO23, GPIO25, and GPIO27 are not exposed on the WROOM-1 module, so SCL0 must move from GPIO22 to GPIO38 and SPI MOSI from GPIO23 to GPIO26. I'll update the documentation and send you the complete revised GPIO table.

value_updates.power_switching: The LED-supplying 5V rail is controlled by ESP32 GPIO5

decisions.reason: Changing the switched-boost enable GPIO does not alter the AXP2101 VMID/VSYS topology.
The battery connector, pinout, placement, and NTC interface are unaffected by the 5V_EN GPIO reassignment.
The battery-protection mechanisms and thresholds do not depend on the switched-boost enable GPIO assignment.
Battery temperature monitoring through the J_BAT NTC is independent of 5V_EN.
The GPIO reassignment does not change the power board's eight-layer stack.
The 5V_EN signal reassignment does not change board dimensions, mounting, orientation, or connector placement.
TVS-based ESD protection remains unchanged by the boost-enable GPIO reassignment.
The USB-C connector's data-line and sourceability requirements are independent of 5V_EN.
This Requirement already has a same-message MODIFY that records 5V_EN on GPIO5, SCL0 on GPIO38, and SPI MOSI on GPIO26.
The source changes control of the separate switched 5V boost rail, not the main board's 3.3V source OR-ing topology or source-selection behavior.
